name: Operation Overlord
notes: Codename of the Allied invasion and campaign in north-west Europe. Wikipedia ends it at the German withdrawal across the Seine, 30 August 1944; some sources end it on 25 August. CMH has no Overlord streamer. An umbrella only: no claim after 30 August 1944 carries it as its operation (the derived operation_name is blank outside these dates), while the Northern France campaign continues to 14 September.

name: Normandy campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 6 June-24 July 1944. The streamer ends the day before Cobra opens (25 July); the first, aborted Cobra bombing was on 24 July.

name: Northern France campaign
parent_date_exception: CMH streamer runs to 14 September; Overlord (Wikipedia) ends 30 August. The campaign is a child of Overlord only for the days both cover; the derived operation_name stops on 30 August.
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 25 July-14 September 1944.

name: Southern France campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 15 August-14 September 1944. Overlaps Northern France by design; a row takes it only through its operation (Dragoon).

name: Rhineland campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 15 September 1944-21 March 1945. Overlaps Ardennes-Alsace; rows of the Ardennes fighting take Ardennes-Alsace through their operation, other rows Rhineland.

name: Ardennes-Alsace campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 16 December 1944-25 January 1945.

name: Central Europe campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 22 March-11 May 1945. Reserved: no claim yet.

name: Operation Neptune
notes: The assault phase of Overlord: the amphibious invasion and the establishment of a foothold. The end date, 30 June 1944, is the date on which Neptune is said to have ended (Wikipedia, Beachhead); the Normandy landings article gives no end date.

name: Operation Tonga
parent_date_exception: The drop began on the night of 5/6 June, before the 6 June start of Neptune and of the Normandy streamer.
notes: British 6th Airborne Division operation on the eastern flank, 5-7 June 1944 (Wikipedia).

name: Operation Perch
notes: British attempt to take Caen from the east, 7-14 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Operation Epsom
notes: British VIII Corps offensive west of Caen, 26-30 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Operation Martlet
notes: British XXX Corps flank operation, 25 June-1 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Carried out in support of Epsom (see data/operation_relations.csv).

name: Battle of Cherbourg
alt_names: Cotentin Peninsula operations; Capture of Cherbourg
notes: Wikipedia dates the Cotentin Peninsula operations 6 June-1 July 1944 and the fight for the city 22-27 June. This row takes the wider window because claims labelled Cherbourg include the VII Corps moves from the Utah landing (7 June) to the capture. Contested boundary: the narrow window would leave 18 earlier claims without this operation.

name: Cutting the Cotentin
notes: VII Corps attack across the base of the Cotentin to cut off the peninsula (Barneville reached 18 June). No source gives the phase a date range: the dates are the span of the narrative in Cross-Channel Attack ch. X and Utah Beach to Cherbourg ch. 8 as used for the five claims.

name: Battle of Carentan
notes: 10-14 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Battle of Bloody Gulch
notes: 13 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); part of the fighting around Carentan.

name: Operation Cobra
notes: 25-31 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Placement: Cobra opened on 25 July, the first day of the Northern France streamer, so it is a child of Northern France, not Normandy (the first bombing, 24 July, was aborted). Decision for the owner if the planned date should count instead.

name: Brittany campaign
parent_date_exception: Ends 19 September with the end of the Brest fighting, after the Northern France streamer ends on 14 September; claims after 14 September take the Rhineland streamer by date.
notes: Third Army operations in Brittany from 1 August 1944 (Third Army operational, Breakout and Pursuit Part Four) to the end of the Brest fighting. Wikipedia gives only "August-September 1944"; the dates are set from the Green Book narrative. Contested.

name: Siege of Brest
notes: Wikipedia: 7 August-20 September 1944. Breakout and Pursuit: the battle ended on 18 September with the surrender of Brest; the Crozon peninsula was cleared on 19 September, which is the end date used. Contested boundary.

name: Battle of Mortain
notes: The Allied side of the German counterattack toward Avranches, 7-13 August 1944. Wikipedia covers it under the German codename, Operation Lüttich.

name: Operation Lüttich
notes: German name of the counterattack at Mortain, 7-13 August 1944. No claim points at this row: it records the German name and links to the Battle of Mortain.

name: Battle of the Falaise Pocket
notes: 12-21 August 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Liberation of Paris
notes: 19-25 August 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Pursuit across France
notes: The drive from the Seine to the German border. No source dates it: the start is the Seine crossing (19 August, Breakout and Pursuit) and the end is the close of the Northern France streamer (14 September; The Siegfried Line Campaign opens on 11 September). Contested; claims labelled Pursuit before 19 August are not matched to it.

name: Operation Dragoon
notes: Allied landings in southern France and the advance up the Rhone valley, 15 August-14 September 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the same dates as the Southern France streamer.

name: Lorraine campaign
notes: Third Army operations in Lorraine, 1 September-18 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox; The Lorraine Campaign opens on 1 September). Spans the Northern France and Rhineland streamers, so it has no parent.

name: Siegfried Line campaign
notes: Wikipedia: 28 August-16 December 1944. The Green Book (The Siegfried Line Campaign) opens with the First Army on 11 September. Spans two streamers, so it has no parent. Contested start.

name: Battle of Aachen
parent_date_exception: Wikipedia dates the battle from 12 September, three days before the Rhineland streamer opens.
notes: 12 September-21 October 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the US assault on the city itself was 2-21 October.

name: Battle of the Scheldt
notes: 2 October-8 November 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Battle of the Vosges
notes: 15 September 1944-15 February 1945 (Wikipedia infobox, a wide span); the claims concern the October-November fighting described in The Riviera to the Rhine ch. 22.

name: Operation Queen
notes: First and Ninth Army offensive toward the Roer, 16 November-16 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Claims labelled Roer in the earlier dataset before 16 November are not matched to it.

name: Operation Clipper
notes: British XXX Corps and US 84th Division attack on Geilenkirchen, 10-22 November 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Operation Market Garden
notes: 17-25 September 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Battle of the Bulge
parent_date_exception: Wikipedia ends the battle on 28 January 1945; the Ardennes-Alsace streamer ends on 25 January.
notes: 16 December 1944-28 January 1945 (Wikipedia infobox). Contested end date.

name: Operation Wacht am Rhein
notes: German codename of the Ardennes offensive. No claim points at this row; it records the German name and links to the Battle of the Bulge.

name: Siege of Bastogne
notes: 20-26 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the relief by Third Army reached the town on 26 December.
